translation.title: Diclofenac Diethylammonium Cream
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and reduction of inflammation in traumatic inflammation of tendons, ligaments, muscles and joints (such as sprains and bruises), localized forms of soft-tissue rheumatism (such as tendovaginitis, shoulder-hand syndrome, bursitis and periarthritis), and localized forms of rheumatic disease (such as osteoarthrosis of the peripheral joints and spine).
translation.usage: Depending on the size of the painful area, apply 2 to 4 g to the affected area 3 to 4 times a day and rub it in gently so that it is absorbed well.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it or have been in the past, if you are hypersensitive to aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, if you have or have had asthma caused by aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (asthma attacks triggered by such medicines), for infants and children 6 years old or younger, in the third trimester of pregnancy, or while breastfeeding. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you are in the first or second trimester of pregnancy, if you are a woman who has difficulty becoming pregnant or is undergoing fertility testing, or for elderly people and children. Do not use it on skin with lesions (bleeding skin disorders, eczema, infected lesions, burns or wounds), or in the eyes or on mucous membranes. Do not use an occlusive (airtight) dressing over it. If you are taking loop diuretics (such as furosemide), thiazide diuretics, medicines that interfere with blood clotting (such as warfarin), antiplatelet medicines (such as aspirin), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, consult a doctor or pharmacist. Adverse reactions may occur - occasionally itching, redness, stinging, dermatitis (rash, eczema, skin eruptions, papules, contact dermatitis, swelling), skin peeling and roughness, irritation and blister formation, and rarely pigmentation; if any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. If serious skin reactions such as exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Using it on damaged skin can cause temporary irritation and a tingling sensation, so use it with care. Store at room temperature.
